question: Which choice most effectively draws on the table's data to complete the text? Effect of Various Soil Treatments on Mean Pineapple Fruit Weight and Size. Table columns: Soil treatment, Weight (grams), Length (centimeters), Diameter (centimeters). Control: 825.9, 6.14, 13.63. Biochar: 915.7, 6.56, 13.63. Compost: 864.8, 6.15, 13.22. Biochar and compost: 979.3, 6.76, 13.68. Biochar and NPK fertilizer: 1032.1, 6.78, 13.96. Working in Ghana, Emmanuel Hanyabui and his colleagues studied how various mixes of soil amendments affected pineapple growth. The additives they tested included NPK fertilizer (a synthetic fertilizer supplying nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium), organic compost, and biochar (a carbon-dense material made from organic waste). According to the table, growers who lack access to inorganic amendments would most likely achieve the greatest increase in their fruits' weight and size by applying ______
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Excluding NPK, the biochar-and-compost combination produces the highest weight (979.3 g) and largest size.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? In Puerto Rico, a city or town is often known by a nickname tied to one of its distinctive traits, such as its scenery, weather, celebrated inhabitants, or main export. Consider the Puerto Rican municipality of Manati, which is famous for having served as a cultural hub during the early 20th ______ this distinction has earned it the fitting nickname of "the Athens of Puerto Rico."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A semicolon correctly joins the two independent clauses on either side of the blank.

question: Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to explain the 50 Completers hiking challenge to a new audience? The Highpointers Club is a club for hikers. A central goal shared by its members is reaching the tallest point in each of the fifty US states. Members who accomplish this are known as 50 Completers. In Suk Han earned the title of 50 Completer on November 15, 2013. West Virginia's highest point is Spruce Knob, at 4,863 ft. Colorado's highest point is Mount Elbert, at 14,440 ft.
option a: Hikers aiming to count themselves among the 50 Completers must reach not only West Virginia's Spruce Knob but also the even higher peak of Mount Elbert in Colorado.
option b: Not until after you have reached the highest points in all fifty US states--including Spruce Knob in West Virginia and Mount Elbert in Colorado--can you include yourself among the 50 Completers of the Highpointers Club.
option c: If you are looking for a new hiking challenge, consider joining the Highpointers Club, as did In Suk Han, a hiker who successfully reached the highest point in every US state.
option d: On November 15, 2013, In Suk Han finally completed the feat of reaching the highest point in all fifty US states, including Spruce Knob in West Virginia and Mount Elbert in Colorado.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice B both defines the 50 Completers and cites Spruce Knob and Mount Elbert as examples for a new audience.

question: Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to introduce Marie Hall to a new audience? Antonio Stradivari (1644-1737), an instrument maker from Italy, crafted roughly 1,000 violins over the course of his life. Musicians treasure his Stradivarius violins for their celebrated tonal quality. The Marie Hall Stradivarius takes its name from a former owner, the British violinist Marie Hall.
option a: Of the 1,000 or so violins Antonio Stradivari made, only about 500 exist today.
option b: Marie Hall was a British violinist who once owned a Stradivarius violin.
option c: The Marie Hall Stradivarius is named after Marie Hall.
option d: Born in 1644, Antonio Stradivari was an Italian instrument maker whose violins are famous for their quality.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice B introduces Marie Hall by identifying her as a British violinist who once owned a Stradivarius.

question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example? Highest Major Summits in India. Table columns: Summit, Elevation (meters), Mountain range, Prominence (meters). Kangto: 7,060, Assam Himalaya, 2,195. Saser Kangri III: 7,495, Saser Karakoram, 850. Langpo: 6,965, Sikkim Himalaya, 560. Sri Kailash: 6,932, Garhwal Himalaya, 1,092. Mount Lakshmi: 6,983, Rimo Karakoram, 800. A mountain summit is commonly described by its elevation, its height above sea level. Yet elevation may be a poorer guide to how tall a peak looks to observers than its prominence, its height above the surrounding terrain, and the two figures can diverge considerably. Consider, for example, the Indian mountain of ______
option a: Saser Kangri III has an elevation of 7,495 meters but a considerably lower prominence of 850 meters.
option b: Kangto has a much higher prominence than does Langpo.
option c: Kangto has a high prominence but is from a different mountain range than Mount Lakshmi, which has a lower prominence.
option d: Sri Kailash has an elevation of 6,932 meters and is considered the highest mountain from the Garhwal Himalaya range.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Saser Kangri III illustrates a high elevation paired with a much lower prominence, the point the example makes.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Charles Dickens's celebrated 1850 novel, which follows a young man called David Copperfield, bears a title that countless readers recognize at once: David Copperfield. Dickens's book, however, originally carried a different ______ while writing and editing, Dickens had planned to call the novel Mag's Diversions.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A semicolon after the parenthetical "though" correctly separates the two independent clauses.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? On Guard is a 1997 photograph by the Iranian artist Shirin Neshat. As in many of Neshat's images, the piece depicts a pair of hands. Gripping a microphone, one hand ______ covered in Persian script, the hands suggest an unseen figure who is on the verge of speaking.
option a: is bare and the other is
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice C keeps the modifying phrase parallel and non-clausal, avoiding a comma splice.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Enormous plumes of dust lifted from the Sahara Desert and carried westward across the Atlantic can produce intricate and conflicting effects on tropical cyclones. For one thing, the dust may encourage the formation of ice clouds within a cyclone's core, boosting precipitation. ______ the dust can also cool the sea surface surrounding the core, sapping the storm's strength.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "On the other hand" signals the opposing, storm-weakening effect that contrasts with the strengthening one.

question: As used in the text, what does the word "consideration" most nearly mean? The following text is adapted from Henry James's 1881 novel The Portrait of a Lady. Everything Osmond did was a pose, a pose so subtly weighed that, unless one were watching closely, one took it for impulse. Ralph had never encountered anyone who dwelt so completely in the land of consideration. His tastes, his studies, his accomplishments, his collections, each served a deliberate end.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Here "consideration" refers to Osmond's careful, deliberate calculation, everything he does serving a purpose.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Regardless of how audiences reacted to Andrew L. Stone's 1943 film Stormy Weather and William Greaves's 1968 film Symbiopsychotaxiplasm, Take One when they first appeared, both movies are now generally viewed quite ______. In 2018, for instance, New York Times critics hailed the former as "[an] anthology of great performances" and the latter as "a vital artifact of its time."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The critics' praise shows the films are now regarded favorably.

question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text? The following text is from Nathaniel Hawthorne's 1830 short story "Sir William Phips." The knowledge handed down by the historian and biographer resembles what we learn of a country from its map, detailed, perhaps, and accurate, and serviceable for every practical need, yet cold and bare, entirely lacking the lifelike charm that landscape painting supplies. Such shortcomings can be partly remedied, and even without truly violating literal truth, though only by means properly forbidden to those who profess biographical exactness.
option a: The more famous a person is, the more likely that person is to attract the attention of a historian.
option b: Biographers are more-skilled writers than other kinds of historians.
option c: Historians' fidelity to the truth often results in work that is less engaging than it could be.
option d: Paintings may be more beautiful than maps, but maps are more useful than paintings.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The passage argues that historians' strict accuracy yields work that is dull and lacking in charm.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? As the anthropologist Cristina Grasseni notes, numerous Italian artisanal cheeses, among them Provolone Valpadana from Trentino-Alto Adige and Ragusano from Sicily, are esteemed for their regional authenticity; ______ they are prized because they are made with local ingredients and by methods characteristic of the particular areas they come from.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "That is" introduces a restatement clarifying what "regional authenticity" means.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? As volcanologists such as Tamsin Mather tend to point out, volcanoes are not all alike. Ischia in Italy, for instance, is a complex volcano, a composite landform made up of related volcanic centers together with their associated lava flows and pyroclastic rock. Mount Vsevidof in Alaska, ______ is a stratovolcano, a cone-shaped volcano built up from many layers of hardened lava and tephra.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "In contrast" marks the difference between Ischia's complex volcano and Vsevidof's stratovolcano.

question: The student wants to provide a historical overview of the Shackleton expedition. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: 1914: British explorer Ernest Shackleton and a small crew set out on an expedition to Antarctica. 1915: Shackleton's ship Endurance became trapped in ice and later broke apart and sank. 1916: After further perilous adventures on the sea ice, the entire crew was rescued. 1959: Historian Alfred Lansing published a book called Endurance: Shackleton's Incredible Voyage. 2001: Filmmaker George Butler released a documentary called The Endurance: Shackleton's Legendary Antarctic Expedition. 2022: The wreck of Endurance was located on the floor of Antarctica's Weddell Sea.
option a: Alfred Lansing wrote about the history of Shackleton's 1914-16 expedition in the book Endurance: Shackleton's Incredible Voyage (1959); years later, in 2001, George Butler released a documentary about the expedition.
option b: In 1914, the Shackleton expedition sailed to Antarctica, where, in 1916, they rescued the crew of a ship that had sunk, Endurance (the wreckage of which was discovered in 2022).
option c: Leaving in 1914 for Antarctica, Shackleton and his crew underwent many harrowing sea-ice adventures, including losing their ship in 1915, before being rescued in 1916.
option d: Shackleton's expedition has inspired a 1959 book, a 2001 film, and a 2022 discovery.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice C gives a chronological overview of the 1914-16 expedition itself, from departure to rescue.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? In a study of how music tempo (measured in beats per minute, or bpm) affects exercise, participants pedaled a stationary bicycle for 30 minutes while continuously hearing Beyonce's "Irreplaceable" (88 bpm). The researchers expected that, when the same participants repeated the activity the next day while listening to Led Zeppelin's "Rock and Roll" (169 bpm), they would pedal faster. Their performance on the second day, however, may have been hampered by fatigue carried over from the first day. Thus, ______
option a: participants demonstrated a preference for one song over the other.
option b: participants' prior familiarity with the songs may have contributed to differences in performance over the two days.
option c: the researchers were unable to accurately measure how quickly participants rode on the second day.
option d: the results from the second day may lead to an underestimation of the effect of the faster song.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Second-day fatigue would suppress performance, causing the faster song's effect to be underestimated.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Robert Louis Stevenson's celebrated 1883 novel, which centers on a young man who finds a treasure map, bears a title that countless readers recognize at once: Treasure Island. Stevenson's book, however, originally carried a different ______ while writing and editing, Stevenson had planned to call the novel The Sea Cook.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A semicolon after the parenthetical "though" correctly separates the two independent clauses.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? ______ the mythological and heroic themes so often present in the work of Thomas Couture and other establishment artists, Konstantin Savitsky's painting Repairing the Railway turns instead to something distinctly ordinary: a large crew of laborers rebuilding damaged train tracks.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Eschewing" means avoiding, matching the contrast with the mundane subject Savitsky chose instead.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Although the musical acts Solido and Banda el Recodo are frequently grouped together under the broad "regional Mexican music" label, each belongs to a separate musical tradition. Solido works within the tejano tradition, which arose in mid-twentieth-century Texas and northern Mexico. Banda el Recodo, ______ follows the banda tradition, whose roots lie in mid-nineteenth-century southern and central Mexico.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "On the other hand" contrasts the banda tradition with the tejano one described before it.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Numerous writings by the Greek historian Strabo (1st century BCE) are ______ his Geographica, a descriptive history of the ancient world, is an extant work: it can still be read.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period splits the two independent clauses, and "Conversely," begins the contrasting one.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? On May 11, 2009, the space shuttle Atlantis lifted off into space, beginning Mission ______ twelve days and twenty-one hours, the mission concluded when the shuttle touched down at Edwards Air Force Base in California.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period ends the first sentence, and the participial phrase "Lasting..." modifies the second.
